title: People Ops: Manager Onboarding, Hiring, Performance & Feedback Playbook
author: Priya Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard practices for manager-led hiring, new manager onboarding, and the performance & feedback cycle. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and engineering managers who run interviews, onboard new hires, and conduct performance reviews.

Scope: Applies to all full-time and long-term contract roles across engineering, product, and go-to-market teams. For VP+ hiring, refer to the Executive Hiring addendum (see related pages).

---

1) Hiring: manager checklist and interview flow

Short intro: Hiring at Redwood balances speed, fairness, and candidate experience. Managers run search, evaluate candidates using structured rubrics, and partner with People Ops for offer and negotiation.

End-to-end hiring steps (numbered):
1. Requisition and role definition
   - Confirm role rationale and team outcomes.
   - Complete Role Brief: responsibilities, success metrics (30/60/90), required skills, compensation band.
   - Obtain hiring approval from director and People Ops (use hiring-approval form).
2. Sourcing and screening
   - Preferred channels: internal referrals, GitHub/ArXiv/OSS, targeted job boards, recruiters for senior roles.
   - Screen candidates with a 20–30 minute phone screen focused on high-level fit and role fundamentals. Use the phone-screen template.
3. Interview loop design
   - Standard loop for IC roles: Recruiter screen -> Manager technical screen -> 2x deep-technical interviews (systems/algorithms or model infra) -> Culture & collaboration -> Hiring manager debrief.
   - Senior or cross-functional roles: add a product/PM or security stakeholder interview.
4. Interview execution and rubrics
   - Use structured scoring 1–5 across core competencies: Technical skill, Problem-solving, Communication, Collaboration, Role-specific knowledge.
   - Interviewers submit written notes within 24 hours.
   - Example rubric (table-style text):
     | Competency | 1 (Below) | 3 (Meets) | 5 (Exceptional) |
     | Technical | Misses key concepts or shows major gaps | Solves core problems with sound reasoning | Demonstrates deep architecture intuition and mentorship |
     | Problem-solving | Unable to decompose problems | Uses sensible heuristics and tradeoffs | Proposes robust, scalable designs across constraints |
5. Debrief and decision
   - Hiring manager runs a 30-minute debrief with interviewers within 48 hours.
   - Tally rubric scores and qualitative signals. People Ops reviews for calibration and equity.
   - Decision recorded in ATS and offer authorization requested.
6. Offer and negotiation
   - People Ops owns offer generation; manager drafts business justification and target comp.
   - Standard negotiation window: 3 business days. Seek People Ops sign-off on exceptions (significant equity or comp stretch).
7. Closing and pre-boarding
   - Confirm start date, send welcome packet, and begin pre-boarding tasks (equipment request, access, first-week calendar).

Hiring SLAs and metrics (bullets):
- Target time-to-offer: 21 business days from first screen to offer for IC roles.
- Recruiter response SLA: initial outreach within 3 business days.
- Interview feedback SLA: notes submitted within 24 hours.
- Diversity: require at least one diverse slate or documentation of outreach for senior roles.

---

2) New manager onboarding (first 90 days)

Goal: Ensure managers at Redwood have the tools, processes, and expectations to onboard reports, run reliable hiring, and manage performance cycles.

Pre-boarding tasks (to be completed before Day 1):
- People Ops: create offer letter, schedule orientation, provision accounts (email, Slack, Google, Okta).
- IT: place hardware order and confirm VPN and MDM enrollment.
- Manager: prepare first-week calendar, 30/60/90 goals template, and introduction message for team.

First week (Day 1–5) checklist:
- Day 1: People Ops orientation (benefits, payroll, policies), IT check-in, security training.
- Day 2–3: Meet direct reports (one-on-ones scheduled), team kickoff meeting, review team OKRs and recent roadmaps.
- Day 4: Product/infra context sessions, access walkthroughs, codebase and deployment overview.
- Day 5: Manager-specific 1:1 with director to align expectations and success metrics.

30/60/90 plan (high-level):
- 30 days: Understand team objectives, people, and tech debt. Conduct introductory 1:1s with each direct report.
- 60 days: Lead first hiring loop or retrospective, set performance priorities, and establish 1:1 cadence.
- 90 days: Drive a small delivery, present hiring roadmap, and complete manager calibration training.

Tools & training resources (bulleted):
- Learning Hub: manager fundamentals training (performance calibration, feedback, coaching).
- HRIS: goal-setting templates and compensation band lookup.
- Playbook: interviewing and inclusive hiring training module.

Manager responsibilities checklist (short bullets):
- Set clear outcomes and success metrics for each direct report.
- Conduct regular, documented 1:1s and career conversations.
- Complete hiring and onboarding tasks on schedule.
- Participate in calibration and promotion panels.

---

3) Performance & feedback cycle

Framework: Redwood runs a continuous feedback model with two formal cycles: mid-year check-in and year-end performance review. Managers are expected to provide ongoing feedback and document conversations.

Cadence and timeline (numbered):
1. Q1 Kickoff: set top-level goals and team OKRs.
2. Continuous feedback: managers and peers give ad-hoc feedback via Slack and the performance tool.
3. Mid-year check-in (June): manager-written summary, 1:1 discussion, and updated 30/60/90s if role changed.
4. Year-end review (December): written review, calibration cycle, promotion/payout decisions, and development plan.

Review components (bullets):
- Manager assessment of role-specific outcomes and competencies.
- Peer feedback summary (collected via the review tool).
- Self-assessment by the employee.
- Calibration notes and final rating.

Ratings and calibration (bulleted):
- Use a 5-point rating scale with defined behavioral anchors.
- Calibration panels led by manager's director and People Ops to ensure consistency across teams.
- Promotions require evidence of sustained impact and manager + panel sign-off.

Feedback best practices for managers (numbered tips):
1. Be timely: give feedback within 72 hours of an observed event when possible.
2. Be specific: cite examples and expected behaviors.
3. Balance: combine appreciations with growth-oriented feedback.
4. Document: summarize important conversations in the performance tool and follow up with next steps.
5. Career-growth: discuss development goals in every 1:1 and build a concrete plan quarterly.

Handling low performance and improvement plans (bulleted):
- For sustained below-expectations performance, managers should:
  - Document instances and coaching attempts.
  - Work with People Ops to design a Performance Improvement Plan (PIP) with clear objectives, timeline (typically 60–90 days), and success criteria.
  - Escalate to director and People Ops if no measurable improvement.

---

4) Manager interview and hiring rubric (appendix)

Interview focus areas (bulleted):
- Technical judgment: ability to assess trade-offs for infra, latency, and cost.
- People leadership: hiring, coaching, career development.
- Operational rigor: incident response, postmortem culture, SLO ownership.
- Cross-team collaboration: product partnerships, customer escalation responses.

Sample manager interview questions (bulleted):
- Describe a time you scaled a team or process to meet increased demand. What trade-offs did you make?
- How do you prioritize technical debt versus feature work in a high-throughput inference platform?
- Tell me about a performance conversation you led that went poorly. What did you learn?
- How do you ensure diverse perspectives during hiring and interviews?

Scoring guidance (bulleted):
- Aim for at least 3 independent interviewers ranking 3+ for an overall hire.
- For promotion into manager roles, include at least one cross-functional interviewer.

---

5) People policies (select highlights)

Probation and confirmation
- Standard probation: 90 days for new hires. Manager completes 30- and 90-day check-ins with People Ops.

Leaves and flexible work
- Redwood supports hybrid remote-first work. Managers should approve work location consistent with team needs and employment laws.
- Standard leaves: parental leave, sick leave, bereavement. Details in the benefits packet.

Promotion and leveling
- Promotions require manager recommendation, peer inputs, and calibration panel sign-off. Provide evidence: impact, leadership, scope expansion, and competency growth.

Compensation and equity
- Compensation bands are published internally; managers may request band exceptions via People Ops.

Confidentiality and data handling
- Managers must treat performance and compensation information as confidential. Share on a need-to-know basis and store documents in the HRIS.

7) Ownership, metrics and continuous improvement

People Ops & manager ownership (bulleted):
- People Ops: process, compliance, offer administration, and training.
- Hiring manager: role definition, interview loop, hiring decision, onboarding execution, and performance conversations.

Key metrics to track (bulleted):
- Time-to-offer (days)
- Offer acceptance rate (%)
- New hire ramp (time to full productivity)
- Manager NPS and new-hire satisfaction (survey)

Continuous improvement loop (numbered):
1. Quarterly review of hiring metrics and candidate experience.
2. Update role templates and rubric adjustments based on calibration outcomes.
3. Run yearly manager training and hiring workshops.

---

FAQ (short)
- Q: When should I open a new requisition?
  A: After you secure budget and director approval. Submit the Role Brief for People Ops review.
- Q: How do I request an exception to comp bands?
  A: Escalate to People Ops with justification and candidate market data.
